evals.name: diverges-candidate-spread
evals.prompt: /planning:brainstorm users keep dropping off during onboarding and we're not sure where to intervene.
evals.expected_output: The skill restates the problem, does a fast codebase grounding pass, and produces a candidate list ordered cheapest to most ambitious — each candidate codebase-grounded (names files/mechanisms it would touch) with effort tier and expected impact — then invites the user to mark what resonates.
expectations: Output produces a list of multiple candidate approaches, not a single chosen solution
The candidates are ordered from cheapest to most ambitious
Each candidate names concrete files or mechanisms it would touch (codebase-grounded), not abstract ideas
Output invites the user to react / mark what resonates rather than committing to one

evals.name: does-not-decide-for-user
evals.prompt: /planning:brainstorm we need to speed up the reports page. Just pick the best approach and tell me which one to do.
evals.expected_output: The skill still produces the cheapest-to-most-ambitious candidate spread and names exactly one recommended option marked (RECOMMENDED) with a basis, but leaves the selection to the user's reaction rather than unilaterally deciding and closing off the alternatives.
expectations: Output presents multiple candidates rather than collapsing to a single answer
Output marks exactly one option as (RECOMMENDED) with a one-line basis
Output leaves the final selection to the user rather than declaring the decision made

evals.name: does-not-self-censor-ambitious-end
evals.prompt: /planning:brainstorm how could we cut our CI runtime — but keep it realistic, I don't want any big rewrites.
evals.expected_output: The candidate list still spans cheapest to most ambitious including the high-effort options; the skill does not pre-filter the ambitious end, letting the user calibrate scope instead of self-censoring.
expectations: Output includes ambitious / high-effort candidates at the ambitious (most-ambitious) end of the spread, not only cheap ones
Output does not silently drop the ambitious options based on the user's aside; it presents them and lets the user calibrate
The spread is still ordered cheapest to most ambitious

evals.name: calibrate-and-route-onward
evals.prompt: /planning:brainstorm ways to add offline support to the mobile app. I've already looked over the candidate space and the two that resonate for me are an outbox/sync-queue approach and a local-first cache. From those two, propose a scope and help me figure out the next step.
evals.expected_output: Given the user's stated resonating candidates, the skill proposes a scope from them and routes onward — to /prd, /interview, /design, or a prototype spike — naming the recommended route marked (RECOMMENDED) with its basis. It does not itself lock scope or start designing.
expectations: Output proposes a downstream route (e.g. /prd, /interview, /design, or a prototype/spike) based on the resonating candidates
The recommended route is marked (RECOMMENDED) with a one-line basis
Output does not itself lock the scope/contract or begin design exploration

evals.name: nothing-rough-open-stops
evals.expected_output: With no argument and no rough problem open in the conversation, the skill says there is nothing rough to diverge on and stops, rather than inventing a problem to brainstorm.
expectations: Output does not fabricate a problem to brainstorm when none is open
Output states that no rough problem is open and stops (or asks the user to supply one)

evals.name: observed-fact-evidence-bar-d5
evals.prompt: /planning:brainstorm we should speed up nightly ETL — I think we need a bigger warehouse or more workers.
evals.expected_output: Produces multiple codebase-grounded candidates where each option cites an observed, falsifiable fact about this repository (a concrete path or mechanism plus a claim that could be wrong), not only a plausible improvement story.
expectations: Each candidate names a concrete file, module, or mechanism in this repo that the option would touch
Each candidate ties the option to an observed fact that could be falsified by reading the codebase, not merely a plausible narrative
Output still presents multiple ordered candidates and invites the user to react rather than picking unilaterally

evals.name: disconnected-scan-before-new-work-d7-d11
evals.prompt: /planning:brainstorm we want notification recipients to get weekly summaries and to see whether a notification was opened. Treat the files under evals/fixtures/disconnected-scan/ as this repository (relative to the skill directory); each carries an added .txt suffix, so app/notifier.py.txt is app/notifier.py.
evals.expected_output: Before proposing new work, the skill scans for what is already built but not connected and reports it as candidates ahead of greenfield options: the unused build_digest import in app/notifier.py (the digest builder exists in app/digest.py), the weekly_digest flag in app/config.py that defaults to False and is never read, and the delivery_receipts table in db/schema.sql that nothing reads or writes. It then invites the user to react.
expectations: Output names the unused build_digest import in app/notifier.py as already-built work that is not connected
Output names the weekly_digest flag in app/config.py as defaulting to off and never read
Output names the delivery_receipts table in db/schema.sql as having no reader
Output reports the disconnected items as candidates ahead of any greenfield option (wire up or enable existing work before building new)
Output ends by inviting the user to react or mark what resonates rather than picking one

evals.name: offers-built-candidate-view
evals.prompt: /planning:brainstorm how could we cut our CI runtime? You gave me twelve candidates, can I tick the ones I like in a page?
evals.expected_output: The skill keeps the numbered candidate list as the record and offers an interactive view built with the checked-in builder from JSON data, candidates ordered cheapest first, with the destination resolved from the medium cascade key.
expectations: The numbered candidate list in the conversation stays the record
The view is built by piping JSON to scripts/build-view.mjs, not by writing HTML or script in the session
The candidates in the view keep the cheapest-to-most-ambitious order of the list
The page is not written into the memory slice, even when brainstorm.md is persisted there
The publish destination comes from the medium key of the rendered-views cascade
